claims.explanation: Fludroxycortide is a glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1) agonist, and its selective antiproliferative/killing pattern across cancer lines is most plausibly explained by glucocorticoid receptor signaling competence: lines with high NR3C1 expression and intact downstream glucocorticoid response (e.g., low NR3C1-repressed AP-1/NF-kB activity) are sensitized, while lines with low NR3C1 or glucocorticoid-resistant drivers (e.g., EGFR/MAPK activation, PTEN loss, mesenchymal/stromal lineages) are protected. The observed enrichment of killing in mesothelioma, pancreatic, melanoma, and breast lines with wild-type or non-EGFR driver profiles, and protection in EGFR-mutant lung, PTEN-mutant glioma/melanoma, and sarcoma lines, is consistent with this. SERPINA6 (CBG) expression may modulate local free drug

features.basis: glucocorticoid receptor is the annotated target; higher receptor expression predicts greater agonist response
corticosteroid-binding globulin sequesters glucocorticoids, reducing free drug available to tumor cells
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, NCIH1437) are among least affected; EGFR/MAPK activation opposes glucocorticoid antiproliferative signaling
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, which antagonizes glucocorticoid-induced apoptosis; PTEN-mutant lines (U118MG, WM793, TE4) are least affected
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines (WM793, K029AX, HS939T) show mixed but overall weaker killing, consistent with MAPK-driven glucocorticoid resistance
KRAS-mutant lines (PATU8988T, LU99, RKN) are among least affected, suggesting RAS/MAPK activation blunts glucocorticoid response
TP53 mutation is common in most killed lines; p53 loss may impair glucocorticoid-induced survival feedback, enhancing killing
ARID1A-mutant lines (LOXIMVI, COLO792, MDAMB175VII) appear enriched among killed lines, possibly via chromatin remodeling altering GR accessibility
NF2-mutant mesothelioma and pancreatic lines (NCIH2052, SNU410) are killed, suggesting Hippo pathway loss sensitizes to glucocorticoids
SMAD4-mutant pancreatic lines (TCCPAN2, ASPC1) are killed, implicating TGF-beta loss in glucocorticoid sensitivity
CDKN2A loss is frequent in killed melanoma and bladder lines, potentially removing a brake on glucocorticoid-induced cell-cycle arrest
PIK3CA-mutant lines (MKN1, BT474, LU99) show mixed response but PI3K activation can oppose glucocorticoid action
